correctness.rationale: Fresh calculus reconstruction confirms all three global minima. With A=sqrt((1-au)^2+b^2), B=sqrt((1+au)^2+b^2), u in (0,1), one has B>A for a,u>0, so I_- > I_+ and J_+=integral w/A > J_-=integral w/B. Since d_b I_±=b J_±, the derivative numerator for I_+/I_- is b(J_+I_- - J_-I_+)>0; adding a positive common constant preserves positivity. For the overlap-inclusive ratio the common term c(b)=sqrt(a^2+b^2)+pi/2 contributes c'(I_--I_+)>0 as well. Thus every ratio is strictly increasing in b and the global problem reduces to b->0+. The boundary formulas split at a=1; the a<=1 branches are decreasing, while for a>1 the substitutions x=asin(1/a) give the stated one-variable derivatives and unique critical equations 2x=pi cos x for lateral/overlap and 2x+pi=2pi cos x for total area. The reported minimizers and values satisfy those equations. Nonattainment follows from b>0.
